svg.title: INTERVIEW CHEAT SHEET: sketchnote
svg.text: Simplest design first → find the number that breaks it → fix only that →
Most of the grade comes from 13–40: show where the simple design breaks, with a number, and fix only that.
Scale: DAU, peak QPS, read:write ratio
Consistency per feature: money CP, feeds AP
Durability: can anything be lost after ack?
Data size and growth per year
Compare each number with one machine: if it fits
with headroom, don't scale it yet.
Too many reads → CDN, cache-aside, replicas
Too many writes → queue, batch, shard, pre-aggregate
Many users, one item → conditional UPDATE, lock + TTL
Steps across services → saga, outbox, idempotency
Big files → presigned multipart upload + CDN
Slow work → queue + workers + job status
"Let me pin down the NFRs with numbers first."
"At 100k reads/s one Postgres falls over, so I
"The timeout means unknown outcome, so we
"One primary handles this write rate, so no
"Delete the cache key on write; it is safe under
"Every write takes an idempotency key, so
"I'll monitor p99, error rate and queue depth."
Kafka, sharding, microservices before the numbers
A Redis lock as the only guard
Say instead: the number, the break, the fix, the trade-off you accept.
"Just add servers" for a hot key
Split the key or cache it locally
This access pattern at this write rate
Cache what can be stale; checkout reads
How do you stop a cache stampede?
Single-flight lock per key (only one request recomputes), jittered TTLs, serve
stale while revalidating, pre-warm hot keys.
Two users book the last seat. What exactly goes wrong and how do you
It blocks on coordinator failure and couples availability.
Write the business row and an event row in one local transaction; a relay/CDC
Delivery is at-least-once in practice; make processing idempotent (dedupe by
ID, upserts) to get an effectively-once result.
Kafka: ordered partitions, replay, multiple consumer groups, stream processing.
How do you make an API retry-safe?
Client-generated Idempotency-Key stored with a unique constraint; return the
Redis lock is enough for correctness?
No. GC pauses or clock issues can leave two holders.
